extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages. It covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval. Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation, as well as catalyze research in universal speech representation learning.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson
extraction.publisher: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S groups several multilingual speech datasets including Fleurs, MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, and Minds-14. For Fleurs, the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark was created using 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets, in 102 languages. Between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence (2.3 on average). New train-dev-test splits were built with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences for train, dev and test respectively. Training sets have around 10 hours of supervision. Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Fleurs is derived from FLoRes machine translation benchmark sentences. MLS is derived from read audiobooks of Librivox. VoxPopuli is derived from European Parliament session recordings. CoVoST-2 is a multilingual speech translation corpus. Minds-14 is extracted from the e-banking domain. Unlabeled speech is available publicly through corpora including MLS, VoxPopuli, CommonVoice. Unlabeled text data is available through Common Crawl data as in the mC4 dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Fleurs, new train-dev-test splits were built with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences for train, dev and test respectively. Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets. For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset, with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. Scripts are provided to download and easily reproduce the preprocessing steps.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For Fleurs, between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence (2.3 on average) from the FLoRes parallel sentences. Speech transcriptions and translations are provided for various tasks.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For Fleurs: between one and three recordings per sentence (2.3 on average)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Datasets and fine-tuning scripts are made easily accessible through the HuggingFace platform. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the Fleurs dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on the platform.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The 102 languages cover various language families and geographical locations including Western Europe/Americas, Eastern Europe, Central-Asia, Middle-East, North-Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, South-East Asia and CJK languages.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group (with 11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli. Reducing the gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. Speech data is not abundant for all languages. The training sets range from a few hours to a few hundred hours of labeled data per language, representing a few-shot setting suited for low-resource understanding. Speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: XTREME-S is designed for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representation learning. Use cases include: Training, Testing, and Validation of multilingual speech models across four task families: speech recognition (ASR), speech-to-text translation (ST), speech classification (LangID and intent classification), and speech retrieval. The benchmark encourages data-efficient self-supervised representation learning. Tasks should be trainable with a reasonable amount of time (few days) and compute (few GPUs). The benchmark is accessible to practitioners working under resource constraints. Users should detail which data they use and settings should be reproducible by the community.
